<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">All of the pretax charges presented above are classified in <span style="font-style:italic;">Impairments &#38; other</span> in the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Statement of Income (Loss)</span>.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>

<td valign="top" style="width:3.33%;white-space:nowrap">

<td valign="top" style="width:3.33%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;</span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;">Geopolitical events that increased the supply of low-priced oil to the global market occurred at the same time that demand weakened due to the worldwide effects of the COVID-19 pandemic, leading to a collapse in oil prices during March 2020.&#160;&#160;As a result, Schlumberger&#8217;s market capitalization deteriorated significantly compared to the end of 2019.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger&#8217;s stock price reached a low during the first quarter of 2020 not seen since 1995.&#160;&#160;Additionally, the Philadelphia Oil Services Sector index, which is comprised of companies involved in the oil services sector, reached an all-time low.&#160;&#160;As a result of these facts, Schlumberger determined that it was more likely than not that the fair value of certain of its reporting units were less than their carrying value.&#160;&#160;Therefore, Schlumberger performed an interim goodwill impairment test.</span></p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger had <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_slbUnit" id="F_000352" name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportingUnits" contextRef="C_0000087347_20200101_20200331" decimals="INF">11</ix:nonFraction> reporting units with goodwill balances aggregating $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000353" name="us-gaap:GoodwillGross" contextRef="C_0000087347_20200331" decimals="-8" scale="9">16.0</ix:nonFraction> billion.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger determined that the fair value of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_slbUnit" id="F_000354" name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportingUnits" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbFourReportingUnitsMember_20200101_20200331" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">four</ix:nonFraction> of its reporting units, representing $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000355" name="us-gaap:GoodwillGross" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbFourReportingUnitsMember_20200331" decimals="-8" scale="9">4.5</ix:nonFraction> billion of the goodwill, was substantially in excess of their carrying value.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger performed a detailed quantitative impairment assessment of the remaining <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_slbUnit" id="F_000356" name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportingUnits" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbSevenReportingUnitsMember_20200101_20200331" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">seven</ix:nonFraction> reporting units, which represented $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000357" name="us-gaap:GoodwillGross" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbSevenReportingUnitsMember_20200331" decimals="-8" scale="9">11.5</ix:nonFraction> billion of goodwill. As a result of this assessment, Schlumberger concluded that the goodwill associated with each of these seven reporting units was impaired, resulting in a $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000358" name="us-gaap:GoodwillAndIntangibleAssetImpairment" contextRef="C_0000087347_20200101_20200331" decimals="-8" scale="9">3.1</ix:nonFraction> billion goodwill impairment charge.&#160;&#160;This charge primarily relates to goodwill associated with the Drilling and Production segments.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Following the $3.1 billion goodwill impairment charge relating to these seven reporting units, <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_slbUnit" id="F_000359" name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportingUnits" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbSixReportingUnitsMember_20200101_20200331" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">six</ix:nonFraction> of these reporting units had a remaining goodwill balance.&#160;&#160;These six reporting units had goodwill balances which ranged between $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000360" name="us-gaap:Goodwill" contextRef="C_0000087347_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbSixReportingUnitsMember_20200331" decimals="-8" scale="9">0.2</ix:nonFraction> billion and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000361" name="us-gaap:Goodwill" contextRef="C_0000087347_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbSixReportingUnitsMember_20200331" decimals="-8" scale="9">5.0</ix:nonFraction> billion and aggregated to $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000362" name="us-gaap:Goodwill" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbSixReportingUnitsMember_20200331" decimals="-8" scale="9">8.4</ix:nonFraction> billion as of March 31, 2020. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">8</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000306_dcnt_4b5a3d94-f8a2-42bb-9519-8b66d15decfd">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger used the income approach to estimate the fair value of its reporting units, but also considered the market approach to validate the results.&#160;&#160;The income approach estimates the fair value by discounting each reporting unit&#8217;s estimated future cash flows using Schlumberger&#8217;s estimate of the discount rate, or expected return, that a marketplace participant would have required as of the valuation date.&#160;&#160;The market approach includes the use of comparative multiples to corroborate the discounted cash flow results.&#160;&#160;The market approach involves significant judgement involved in the selection of the appropriate peer group companies and valuation multiples.</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Some of the more significant assumptions inherent in the income approach include the estimated future net annual cash flows for each reporting unit and the discount rate.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger selected the assumptions used in the discounted cash flow projections using historical data supplemented by current and anticipated market conditions and estimated growth rates.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger&#8217;s estimates are based upon assumptions believed to be reasonable.&#160;&#160;However, given the inherent uncertainty in determining the assumptions underlying a discounted cash flow analysis, particularly in the current volatile market, actual results may differ from those used in Schlumberger&#8217;s valuations which could result in additional impairment charges in the future.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The discount rates utilized to value Schlumberger&#8217;s reporting units were between <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000363" name="slb:DiscountRateUtilized" contextRef="C_0000087347_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_20200101_20200331" decimals="3" scale="-2">12.0</ix:nonFraction>% and <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000364" name="slb:DiscountRateUtilized" contextRef="C_0000087347_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20200101_20200331" decimals="3" scale="-2">13.5</ix:nonFraction>%, depending on the risks and uncertainty inherent in the respective reporting unit as well as the size of the reporting unit.&#160;&#160;Assuming all other assumptions and inputs used in each of the respective discounted cash flow analysis were held constant, a <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000365" name="slb:ExpectedIncreaseDecreaseInDiscountRateAssumption" contextRef="C_0000087347_20200101_20200331" decimals="4" scale="-4">50</ix:nonFraction>-basis point increase or decrease in the discount rate assumptions would have changed the fair value of the <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_slbUnit" id="F_000366" name="slb:NumberOfReportingUnitsFairValueToBeImpacted" contextRef="C_0000087347_20200101_20200331" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">seven</ix:nonFraction> reporting units, on average, by less than <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000367" name="slb:ExpectedPercentageChangeInFairValueOfReportingUnits" contextRef="C_0000087347_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20200101_20200331" decimals="2" scale="-2">5</ix:nonFraction>%.</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">At March 31, 2020, Schlumberger had separate committed credit facility agreements aggregating $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000579" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" contextRef="C_0000087347_20200331" decimals="-7" scale="9">6.25</ix:nonFraction> billion with commercial banks, of which $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000580" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityRemainingBorrowingCapacity" contextRef="C_0000087347_20200331" decimals="-8" scale="9">3.5</ix:nonFraction> billion was available and unused.&#160;&#160;&#160;These committed facilities support commercial paper programs in the United States and Europe, of which $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000581" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_slbCommercialPaperProgramsMaturingFebruaryTwoZeroTwoThreeMember_20200331" decimals="-7" scale="9">2.75</ix:nonFraction> billion matures in February 2023, $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000582" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_slbCommercialPaperProgramsMaturingJulyTwoZeroTwoFourMember_20200331" decimals="-8" scale="9">1.5</ix:nonFraction> billion matures in July 2024 and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000583" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_slbCommercialPaperProgramsMaturingFebruaryTwoZeroTwoFiveMember_20200331" decimals="-8" scale="9">2.0</ix:nonFraction> billion matures in February 2025.&#160;&#160;Interest rates and other terms of borrowing under these lines of credit vary by facility.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Subsequent to the end of the first quarter of 2020, Schlumberger entered into a &#8364;<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217EUR" id="F_000584" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_20200331" decimals="-8" scale="9">1.2</ix:nonFraction> billion committed revolving credit facility.&#160;&#160;This <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_000585">one-year</span> facility can be extended at Schlumberger&#8217;s option for up to an additional year.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger can potentially upsize this facility through syndication.&#160;&#160;As of April 22, 2020, <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000586" name="slb:CreditFacilityWithdrawalAmount" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_us-gaapSubsequentEventTypeAxis_us-gaapSubsequentEventMember_20200422_20200422" decimals="-6" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="6">no</ix:nonFraction> amounts have been drawn under this facility.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Borrowings under the commercial paper programs at March 31, 2020 were $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000587" name="us-gaap:LongTermDebt" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_us-gaapCommercialPaperMember_20200331" decimals="-7" scale="9">2.75</ix:nonFraction> billion, all of which&#160;was classified in&#160;<span style="font-style:italic;">Long-term debt</span> in the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Balance </span><span style="color:#000000;">Sheet</span>.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2019, borrowings under the commercial paper programs were $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000588" name="us-gaap:LongTermDebt" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_us-gaapCommercialPaperMember_20191231" decimals="-8" scale="9">2.2</ix:nonFraction>2 billion, all of which was classified in <span style="font-style:italic;">Long-term debt</span> in the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Balance Sheet</span>.</p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">12</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000313" name="us-gaap:DerivativeInstrumentsAndHedgingActivitiesDisclosureTextBlock" contextRef="C_0000087347_20200101_20200331" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000313_dcnt_706e3f71-825c-4167-9d20-a9e0e681757a">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">9.&#160;&#160; <span style="text-decoration:underline;">Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities</span> </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger is exposed to market risks related to fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates and interest rates.&#160; To mitigate these risks, Schlumberger utilizes derivative instruments.&#160; Schlumberger does not enter into derivative transactions for speculative purposes. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Interest Rate Risk </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger is subject to interest rate risk on its debt and its investment portfolio.&#160; Schlumberger maintains an interest rate risk management strategy that uses a mix of variable and fixed rate debt combined with its investment portfolio, to mitigate the exposure to changes in interest rates.&#160; </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">At March 31, 2020, Schlumberger had fixed rate debt aggregating $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000589" name="slb:FixedRateDebt" contextRef="C_0000087347_20200331" decimals="-8" scale="9">13.7</ix:nonFraction> billion and variable rate debt aggregating $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000590" name="slb:VariableRateDebt" contextRef="C_0000087347_20200331" decimals="-8" scale="9">2.9</ix:nonFraction> billion. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Foreign Currency Exchange Rate Risk </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As a multinational company, Schlumberger generates revenue in more than <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_slbCountry" id="F_000591" name="us-gaap:NumberOfCountriesInWhichEntityOperates" contextRef="C_0000087347_20200331" decimals="INF">120</ix:nonFraction> countries. Schlumberger&#8217;s functional currency is primarily the US dollar.&#160; However, outside the United States, a significant portion of Schlumberger&#8217;s expenses are incurred in foreign currencies.&#160; Therefore, when the US dollar weakens (strengthens) in relation to the foreign currencies of the countries in which Schlumberger conducts business, the US dollar-reported expenses will increase (decrease).&#160;&#160; </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger is exposed to risks on future cash flows to the extent that the local currency is not the functional currency and expenses denominated in local currency are not equal to revenues denominated in local currency.&#160;&#160;&#160; Schlumberger uses foreign currency forward contracts to provide a hedge against a portion of these cash flow risks.&#160; These contracts are accounted for as cash flow hedges, with the changes in the fair value of the hedge recorded on the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Balance Sheet </span>and in <span style="font-style:italic;">Accumulated Other Comprehensive Loss.&#160; </span>Amounts recorded in<span style="font-style:italic;"> Accumulated Other Comprehensive Loss </span>are reclassified into earnings in the same period or periods that the hedged item is recognized in earnings.&#160; </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger is also exposed to risks on future cash flows relating to certain of its fixed rate debt denominated in currencies other than the functional currency. Schlumberger uses cross-currency swaps to provide a hedge against these cash flow risks. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: the fair value of its $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000594" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" <p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">At March 31, 2020, contracts were outstanding for the US dollar equivalent of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000619" name="us-gaap:DerivativeNotionalAmount" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapDerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis_us-gaapForeignExchangeContractMember_20200331" decimals="INF" scale="9">7.3</ix:nonFraction> billion in various foreign currencies, of which $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000620" name="us-gaap:DerivativeNotionalAmount" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapDerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis_us-gaapForeignExchangeContractMember_us-gaapFinancialInstrumentAxis_us-gaapDebtMember_us-gaapHedgingDesignationAxis_us-gaapDesignatedAsHedgingInstrumentMember_20200331" decimals="INF" scale="9">4.0</ix:nonFraction> billion relates to hedges of debt denominated in currencies other than the functional currency. </p></ix:nonNumeric>

<td valign="top" style="width:4.54%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><sup style="font-size:85%;line-height:120%;vertical-align:top">(4)</sup></span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">Charges and credits are described in detail in Note 2 to the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Financial Statements.</span></p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">First-quarter revenue of $7.5 billion declined 9% sequentially and 5% year-on-year as the unprecedented global health and economic crisis sparked by the COVID-19 pandemic increasingly impacted industry activity during the quarter. The effect of this was amplified late in the quarter by a new battle for market share between the world&#8217;s largest oil producers. This created simultaneous shocks in oil supply and demand resulting in the most challenging industry environment in many decades. The spread of COVID-19 has caused more than 50 countries to implement lockdown measures affecting three billion people. Worldwide economic activity is falling sharply, and oil demand destruction is leading to an unprecedented supply-demand imbalance in the range of 20&#8211;30 million bbl/d. This is translating to near-term uncertainties in activity and budget projections.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Customer spending and drilling activity in North America declined as oil prices slipped early in the quarter before falling abruptly in March. This resulted in a 7% sequential decrease in North America revenue to $2.3 billion. International activity, which was expected to be seasonally lower sequentially, suffered from COVID-19-related activity disruptions and initial customer spending cuts in response to falling oil prices. International revenue of $5.1 billion declined 10% sequentially.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The sequential international revenue decline was led by lower winter activity in the Europe/CIS/Africa area, particularly in the Russia &#38; Central Asia and the United Kingdom &#38; Continental Europe GeoMarkets. Latin America area revenue also decreased, mainly due to reduced WesternGeco<sup style="font-size:85%;line-height:120%;vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup> multiclient seismic license sales. Middle East &#38; Asia area revenue declined on lower product sales following strong year-end sales and a seasonal decline in activity. COVID-19-related activity disruptions during the quarter impacted our operations, particularly in China, Malaysia, Iraq, Italy, Romania, the United Kingdom, Gabon, Mozambique, Congo, Nigeria, Angola, and offshore North America.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">At this time, customer feedback and Schlumberger&#8217;s analysis indicate global capex spend is expected to decline by about 20% in 2020, with the largest share of the reduction affecting North America, which is estimated to drop by about 40%. In contrast, international E&#38;P capex is expected to decline by about 15%. &#160;Final investment decision sanctions are expected to fall back to trough levels of 2015, which would indicate project delays to 2021 and beyond.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">17</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In this environment&#8212;the duration of which remains uncertain&#8212;Schlumberger has planned for a range of scenarios and </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">has</span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">taken a number of actions. To protect its workforce in the wake of COVID-19, Schlumberger has taken steps to keep its people safe by supporting those affected, mandating that as many employees and contractors as possible work from home, and monitoring those who cannot do so and are required to be at work. To reinforce cost control and cash discipline, Schlumberger is reducing its structural and variable costs, and restructuring its organization to match activity where necessary, including furloughing personnel, cutting salaries, lowering headcount, and closing facilities. </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Additionally, Schlumberger's </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Board of Directors</span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">and executive officers have voluntarily agreed to reductions in their cash compensation.&#160;&#160;</span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The capital investment program has been reduced by more than 30% and </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">resources will be allocated</span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> to the more resilient markets while Schlumberger remains focused on capital stewardship and maintaining its commitment to a strong balance sheet. </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The second quarter is likely to be the most uncertain and disruptive quarter the industry has ever seen.&#160;&#160;The extent to which Schlumberger&#8217;s future results are affected by COVID-19 will depend on various factors and consequences beyond the Company&#8217;s control, such as the duration and scope of the pandemic&#59; additional actions by businesses and governments in response to the pandemic, and the speed and effectiveness of responses to combat the virus. COVID-19, and the volatile regional and global economic conditions stemming from the pandemic, could also aggravate the risk factors identified in Schlumberger&#8217;s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2019. COVID-19 may also materially adversely affect Schlumberger&#8217;s results in a manner that is either not currently known or that Schlumberger does not currently consider to be a significant risk to its business.&#160;&#160;See also the risk factor relating to COVID-19 disclosed in Item 8.01 of Schlumberger&#8217;s Current Report on Form 8-K filed on April 17, 2020.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Reservoir Characterization </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Reservoir Characterization revenue of $1.3 billion decreased 20% sequentially.&#160;&#160;This decrease was primarily due to seasonally lower sales of software and multiclient seismic licenses and reduced winter activity in the Northern Hemisphere.&#160;&#160;Additionally, customers began to cut both discretionary spend and activity toward the end of the quarter, which affected exploration activity in several GeoMarkets. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Reservoir Characterization pretax operating margin of 14% fell 839 basis points (&#8220;bps&#8221;) sequentially due to the lower sales of software and multiclient seismic licenses as well as the effects of lower exploration activity.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Drilling </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Drilling revenue of $2.3 billion decreased 6% sequentially with a<span style="color:#000000;">pproximately half of the revenue decline attributable </span>to the divestiture of the businesses and associated assets of DRILCO, Thomas Tools, and Fishing &#38; Remedial Services (the &#8220;Drilling Tools businesses&#8221;) which was completed at the end of the fourth quarter of 2019.&#160;&#160;Revenue also decreased due to seasonality effects in the Northern Hemisphere. The <span style="color:#000000;">US land rig count was 6% lower sequentially including a 15% drop in the last two weeks of March.&#160;&#160; </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Drilling pretax operating margin of 12% was resilient, as it remained flat with the previous quarter despite the sequential revenue decline as profitability was boosted by the <span style="color:#000000;">divestiture of the </span>Drilling Tools<span style="color:#000000;"> businesses, which were previously dilutive to margins.</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Production </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Production revenue of $2.7 billion declined 6% sequentially.<span style="color:#000000;"> </span>This was driven by lower Well Services activity and weaker Artificial Lift Solutions sales in the international markets. <span style="color:#000000;">OneStim</span><sup style="font-size:85%;line-height:120%;vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup><span style="color:#000000;"> revenue grew slightly as its scale-to-fit strategy successfully generated higher fleet utilization, however activity fell sharply in mid-March as customers cut their spending. OneStim began to stack more frac fleets in response and have reduced their active fleets by 27% during March.</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Production pretax operating margin of 8% contracted by 98 bps sequentially due to reduced profitability in North America while international margins were flat despite lower revenue. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Cameron </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Cameron revenue of $1.3 billion decreased 10% sequentially mostly due to lower revenue in North America from the short-cycle businesses of Surface Systems and Valves &#38; Process Systems. Revenue was impacted by the temporary closure of manufacturing facilities in Italy and Malaysia caused by COVID-19-related disruptions that impacted OneSubsea<sup style="font-size:85%;line-height:120%;vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup>, Surface Systems, and Valves &#38; Process Systems activity.<sup style="font-size:85%;line-height:120%;vertical-align:top"> </sup></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Cameron pretax operating margin of 10% improved slightly by 57 bps.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">18</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:2pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">First Quarter 2020 Compared to First Quarter 2019</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p></td>
<td valign="bottom" style="background-color:#FFFFFF;padding-left:0pt;padding-Right:0.75pt;padding-Top:0.75pt;padding-Bottom:0pt;width:1%;white-space:nowrap;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p></td>
<td valign="bottom" style="background-color:#FFFFFF;padding-left:0pt;padding-Right:0.75pt;padding-Top:0.75pt;padding-Bottom:0pt;width:9.32%;white-space:nowrap;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p></td>
<td valign="bottom" style="background-color:#FFFFFF;padding-left:0pt;padding-Right:0.75pt;padding-Top:0.75pt;padding-Bottom:0pt;width:1%;white-space:nowrap;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p></td>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#auto;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">First-quarter 2020 revenue of $7.5 billion decreased 5% year-on-year as customers began to cut spending in response to falling oil prices caused by the simultaneous shocks in oil supply and demand due to the unprecedented global health and economic crisis sparked by the COVID-19 pandemic. North America revenue declined 17% year-on-year. The international business showed some resilience as revenue increased 2% year-on-year against the backdrop of an increasingly difficult operating environment.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Reservoir Characterization </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">First-quarter 2020 revenue of $1.3 billion <span style="color:#auto;">fell 10% year-on-year as customers began to cut discretionary spending, which caused a reduction in exploration activity that impacted Wireline, WesternGeco, and Software Integrated Solutions (&#8220;SIS&#8221;). Activity was also lower in a number of countries affected by COVID-19-related disruptions. </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#auto;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Year-on-year, pretax operating margin dropped 525 bps year-on-year to 14% due to lower high-margin exploration activity. Lower sales of SIS software and WesternGeco multiclient seismic licenses also contributed to the year-on-year margin contraction.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Drilling </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">First-quarter <span style="color:#auto;">2020 revenue of $2.3 billion decreased 4% year-on-year largely due to the divestiture of the Drilling Tools businesses at the end of the fourth quarter of 2019. Revenue also declined due to the significant drop in rig count in North America as customers reduced spending due to falling oil prices. Internationally, activity was also reduced in a number of countries in the Middle East &#38; Asia and Europe/CIS/Africa areas impacted by COVID-19-related disruptions. </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#auto;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Year-on-year, pretax operating margin decreased 42 bps to 12%. While margins were lower due to the decrease in revenue and COVID-19-related disruptions, profitability was boosted by the divestiture of the Drilling Tools businesses which was previously dilutive to margins.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">19</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Production </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">First-quarter <span style="color:#auto;">2020 revenue of $2.7 billion</span> <span style="color:#auto;">decreased 6% year-on-year primarily due to lower OneStim revenue as customers in North America land continued to decrease their investment spending resulting in the stacking of additional fleet capacity. </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#auto;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Year-on-year, pretax operating margin increased by 32 bps to 8% as improved margins in Asset Performance Solutions (&#8220;APS&#8221;) internationally were largely offset by reduced profitability in OneStim in North America land.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Cameron </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">First-quarter 2020 revenue of $1.3 billion was essentially flat compared to the same period in 2019, as revenue growth from the long cycle businesses of OneSubsea and Drilling Systems was offset by a revenue decline in Valves &#38; Process Systems. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Year-on-year, pretax operating margin decreased 209 bps to 10% primarily driven by reduced profitability in the short cycle businesses of Surface Systems and Valves &#38; Process Systems. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Interest and Other Income</span></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The first quarter 2020 results did not include any benefit from reduced depreciation and amortization expense as a result of the first quarter impairment charges.&#160;&#160;However, going forward, depreciation and amortization expense will be reduced by approximately $95 million on a quarterly basis.&#160;&#160;Approximately $45 million of this quarterly reduction will be reflected in the Production segment, with the remaining $50 million reflected in the &#8220;Corporate &#38; other&#8221; line item. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">There were no charges or credits recorded during the first quarter of 2019.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger expects to record a significant charge relating to severance during the second quarter of 2020.&#160;&#160;However, at this time the amount cannot be reasonably estimated.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Liquidity and Capital Resources</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The <span style="color:#000000;">effects of the COVID-19 pandemic have resulted in a significant and swift reduction in international and U.S. economic activity. These effects have adversely affected the demand for oil and natural gas, as well as for Schlumberger&#8217;s products and services, and </span>caused significant volatility and disruption of the financial markets. This period of extreme economic disruption, low oil prices and reduced demand for Schlumberger&#8217;s products and services has had, and is likely to continue to have, a material adverse impact on our business, results of operations, access to sources of liquidity and financial condition. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In view of the uncertainty of the depth and extent of the contraction in oil demand due to the COVID-19 pandemic combined with the weaker commodity price environment, Schlumberger has turned its strategic focus to cash conservation and protecting its balance sheet. Schlumberger therefore reduced its dividend by 75%, commencing with the next dividend payment in July 2020. The revised dividend supports Schlumberger&#8217;s value proposition through a balanced approach of shareholder distributions and organic investment, while providing the flexibility to weather the uncertain environment. This decision reflects the Company&#8217;s focus on its capital stewardship program as well as its commitment to maintain both a strong liquidity position and a strong investment grade credit rating that provides privileged access to the financial markets.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Details of the components of liquidity as well as changes in liquidity follow:<span style="font-size:12pt;">&#160;</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:2pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">&#8220;Free cash flow&#8221; represents cash flow from operations less capital expenditures, APS investments and multiclient seismic data costs capitalized. Management believes that free cash flow is an important liquidity measure for the company and that it is useful to investors and management as a measure of our ability to generate cash.&#160;&#160;Once business needs and obligations are met, this cash can be used to reinvest in the company for future growth or to return to shareholders through dividend payments or share repurchases.&#160;&#160;Free cash flow does not represent the residual cash flow available for discretionary expenditures.&#160;&#160;Free cash flow is a non-GAAP financial measure that should be considered in addition to, not as substitute for or superior to, cash flow from operations. </p></td></tr></table></div>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger generates revenue in more than 120 countries.&#160;&#160;&#160;As of March 31, 2020, four of those countries individually accounted for greater than 5% of Schlumberger&#8217;s net receivables balance, of which only the United States accounted for greater than 10% of such receivables.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of March 31, 2020, Schlumberger had $3.3 billion of cash and short-term investments on hand.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger had separate committed debt facility agreements aggregating $6.3 billion that support commercial paper programs, of which $3.5 billion was available and unused.&#160;&#160;Additionally, subsequent to the end of the first quarter of 2020, Schlumberger entered into a &#8364;1.2 billion committed revolving credit facility.&#160;&#160;This one-year facility can be extended at Schlumberger&#8217;s option for up to an additional year.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger can potentially upsize this facility through syndication.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger believes these amounts are sufficient to meet future business requirements for at least the next 12 months. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Borrowings under the commercial paper programs at March 31, 2020 were $2.8 billion.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">FORWARD-LOOKING STATEMENTS</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">This first-quarter 2020 Form 10-Q, as well as other statements we make, contain &#8220;forward-looking statements&#8221; within the meaning of the federal securities laws, which include any statements that are not historical facts, such as our forecasts or expectations regarding business outlook&#59; growth for Schlumberger as a whole and for each of its segments (and for specified products or geographic areas within each segment)&#59; oil and natural gas demand and production growth&#59; oil and natural gas prices&#59; improvements in operating procedures and technology, including our transformation program&#59; capital expenditures by Schlumberger and the oil and gas industry&#59; the business strategies of Schlumberger&#8217;s customers&#59; our effective tax rate&#59; future global economic conditions&#59; and future results of operations. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties, including, but not limited to, changing global economic conditions&#59; public health crises, such as the COVID-19 pandemic, and any related actions taken by businesses and governments&#59; changes in exploration and production spending by Schlumberger&#8217;s customers and changes in the level of oil and natural gas exploration and development&#59; the results of operations and financial condition of Schlumberger&#8217;s customers and suppliers, particularly during extended periods of low prices for crude oil and natural gas&#59; general economic, political, and business conditions in key regions of the world&#59; foreign currency risk&#59; pricing pressure&#59; weather and seasonal factors&#59; operational modifications, delays or cancellations&#59; production declines&#59; changes in government regulations and regulatory requirements, including those related to offshore oil and gas exploration, radioactive sources, explosives, chemicals, hydraulic fracturing services and climate-related initiatives&#59; the inability of technology to meet new challenges in exploration&#59; the competitiveness of alternate-energy sources or product substitutes&#59; and other risks and uncertainties detailed in this Form 10-Q and our most recent Form 10-K and Form 8-K filed with or furnished to the SEC. If one or more of these or other risks or uncertainties materialize (or the consequences of any such development changes), or should our underlying assumptions prove incorrect, actual outcomes may vary materially from those reflected in our forward-looking statements. Statements in this first-quarter 2020 Form 10-Q are made as of April 22, 2020, and Schlumberger disclaims any intention or obligation to update publicly or revise such statements, whether as a result of new information, future events or otherwise.</p>

Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures about Market Risk. </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">For quantitative and qualitative disclosures about market risk affecting Schlumberger, see Item&#160;7A, &#8220;Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures about Market Risk,&#8221; of the Schlumberger Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December&#160;31, 2019. Schlumberger&#8217;s exposure to market risk has not changed materially since December&#160;31, 2019.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="Item_4_Controls_and_Procedures"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Item&#160;4. Controls and Procedures. </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger has carried out an evaluation under the supervision and with the participation of Schlumberger&#8217;s management, including the Chief Executive Officer (&#8220;CEO&#8221;) and the Chief Financial Officer (&#8220;CFO&#8221;), of the effectiveness of Schlumberger&#8217;s &#8220;disclosure controls and procedures&#8221; (as such term is defined in Rules 13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e) under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the &#8220;Exchange Act&#8221;)) as of the end of the period covered by this report. Based on this evaluation, the CEO and the CFO have concluded that, as of the end of the period covered by this report, Schlumberger&#8217;s disclosure controls and procedures were effective to provide reasonable assurance that information required to be disclosed in the reports that Schlumberger files or submits under the Exchange Act is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in the Securities and Exchange Commission&#8217;s rules and forms. Schlumberger&#8217;s disclosure controls and procedures include controls and procedures designed to ensure that information required to be disclosed in reports filed or submitted under the Exchange Act is accumulated and communicated to its management, including the CEO and the CFO, as appropriate, to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure. There was no change in Schlumberger&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting during the quarter to which this report relates that has materially affected, or is reasonably likely to materially affect, Schlumberger&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting.</p>

Defaults Upon Senior Securities. </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">None<span style="font-weight:bold;">. </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="Item_4_Mine_Safety_Disclosures"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Item&#160;4. Mine Safety Disclosures. </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our mining operations are subject to regulation by the federal Mine Safety and Health Administration under the Federal Mine Safety and Health Act of 1977. Information concerning mine safety violations or other regulatory matters required by section 1503(a) of the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act and Item&#160;104 of Regulation S-K is included in Exhibit 95 to this report.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="Item_5_Other_Information"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Item&#160;5. Other Information. </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In 2013, Schlumberger completed the wind down of its service operations in Iran. Prior to this, certain non-US subsidiaries provided oilfield services to the National Iranian Oil Company and certain of its affiliates (&#8220;NIOC&#8221;).</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger&#8217;s residual transactions or dealings with the government of Iran during the first quarter of 2020 consisted of payments of taxes and other typical governmental charges. Certain non-US subsidiaries of Schlumberger maintain depository accounts at the Dubai branch of Bank Saderat Iran (&#8220;Saderat&#8221;), and at Bank Tejarat (&#8220;Tejarat&#8221;) in Tehran and in Kish for the deposit by NIOC of amounts owed to non-US subsidiaries of Schlumberger for prior services rendered in Iran and for the maintenance of such amounts previously received. One non-US subsidiary also maintained an account at Tejarat for payment of local expenses such as taxes. Schlumberger anticipates that it will discontinue dealings with Saderat and Tejarat following the receipt of all amounts owed to Schlumberger for prior services rendered in Iran.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">25</p>
